reasoning.step1:
1) Document classification
- Contains clear invoice indicators: title "Rechnung", "Gesamtsumme", "Rechnungsbetrag", invoice-like headers, line items and totals. No exclusion headers like "Mahnung" or "Zahlungserinnerung". => Classified as invoice.

2) Identify candidate fields in text
- Invoice date: multiple "v. 30.01.2024" near Belegnr./Lieferschein/Auftrag; invoice header shows "Belegnr. 31695933 v. 30.01.2024". Use "30.01.2024" as Invoice.Date.
- Grand total: "Rechnungsbetrag 4.789,99" on page 2. European format uses comma as decimal separator; numeric value = 4789.99.
- Net amount: "Gesamtbetrag exkl. Umsatzsteuer 4.354,54" => Net = 4354.54.
- VAT amount: "Umsatzsteuer 10,00% von 4.354,54 435,45" => VAT amount = 435.45.
- VAT rate: "10,00%" shown; per rule strip percent symbol => 10.
- Sender VAT ID: two UIDs present: "UID: ATU22642807" appears with the Rechnungsempfänger (customer BÄKO). Footer shows sender details including "UID: ATU23264205" for NÖM AG (sender). Per schema Sender.VatId = ATU23264205.

3) Verify no inference beyond text
- All extracted values are explicitly present in the invoice text; no guessed data.
- Decimal formats preserved: 4.789,99 -> 4789.99; 4.354,54 -> 4354.54; 435,45 -> 435.45; VAT rate preserved as 10.

4) Multiple occurrences / ambiguity handling
- Two UID occurrences distinguished by context (recipient vs sender); selected sender UID from sender block.
- Invoice date occurrence consistent across document; selected date appearing with Belegnr. and invoice header.

Conclusion: fields to extract — Invoice.Date = "30.01.2024"; GrandTotal.Amount = 4789.99; Net.Amount = 4354.54; Vat.Amount = 435.45; Vat.Rate = 10; Sender.VatId = "ATU23264205".
